brief: Retained mansion brief; offline mock decisions, not a model-produced revision

intent.thesis: A Caribbean belvedere estate organized as a ceremonial arrival plinth, a broad ocean-facing social salon, a lower guest wing, and a more secluded elevated family-and-owner pavilion. Deep limestone terraces frame the sea-facing edge while warm timber, ivory render, bronze openings, and sage-toned screened service volumes give the composition a refined tropical character without relying on ornamental facade detail.

masses.role: A low, processional limestone arrival court that establishes a memorable threshold from the landward side.
The principal double-aspect entertaining volume, opening from arrival through to the waterfront terrace.
A long, quieter east wing containing three generous guest-suite allocations and their private internal threshold sequence.
An open-roof lower stair court capped by an upper stair lantern, joining the social level to the private pavilion.
An elevated family gallery with owner and family suite allocations, set back behind a substantial sky terrace.

limitations: The proposal is a supported semantic architectural study, not a verified US$25 million valuation, complete construction package, or claim of a finished premium residence.

The requested infinity pool is not represented: pool basins, hydraulic edges, water, equipment, and detailed pool-deck construction are outside the supported geometry. The ocean terrace reserves the appropriate waterfront social interface only.
Tropical planting, landscape design, terrain shaping, retaining, site grading, and a literal response to the gently sloping Saint Lucia site are omitted; all represented spaces use a common datum.
Only separate flat polygon roofs are represented. Pitched, sculptural, overhanging, and otherwise advanced roof forms are omitted.

Facade articulation beyond the selected material intent, including shading systems, screens, balustrades, guards, ordinary elevated-sill windows, exterior lighting, and detailed joinery, remains unresolved.

The six suite allocations establish architectural area and circulation intent only. Bathrooms, wardrobes, furniture, fixtures, kitchens, service rooms, acoustic separation, and all detailed interior fit-out remain unfinished.

Guest and family suite privacy is expressed through wing hierarchy and suite-threshold sequencing, but internal suite vestibules, bathrooms, and secondary private corridors require later detailed planning.
Structural design, foundations, hurricane and coastal-resilience design, MEP systems, drainage, code review, accessibility review, permits, and waterfront approvals are unresolved.

instructions: Return one complete semantic proposal using the existing schema. Make only explicit architectural choices in editableIds; coordinate their entire dependency group. Preserve identities, concept, programme, mass roles, frame, access obligations and limitations. Offsets are metres from the host edge start. Do not infer normalized offsets, bridge gaps or invent intent. If the supported straight stair, full-edge topology or preserved programme prevents a valid design, return decision-required with a broader redesign request. No scene geometry is committed until the entire revised proposal compiles and passes sampled physical checks. Alternatives in findings are options, never selected repairs.
